items.editor_note: Targets multi-hop RAG by training the embedding retriever on its own failures.

items.editor_note: Frames current RAG as unsatisfactory and proposes TRIO for task refinement.

items.title: Compaction, decay and reinforcement in a two-tier conversational memory: a paired evaluation against retrieval-augmented generation
items.summary_1line: A conversational agent that remembers has to decide what to keep. Retrieval-augmented generation keeps the transcript and searches it; the alternative is to compact each turn into atomic facts and search those. We com...
items.editor_note: Moves the question from retrieval to memory: transcript search versus compacted atomic facts.

editorial.tldr: Late-October research targeted the retriever: a paper trained embedding models on their own mistakes so multi-hop questions find all the evidence they need. A November 2 paper, TRIO, then argued that current RAG approaches are still far from satisfactory.
editorial.whats_new: A Nov 6 paper compares RAG over a raw transcript against a two-tier memory that compacts each turn into atomic facts, testing whether conversational agents should keep the transcript at all.
editorial.why_it_matters: RAG design choices (what you index, how the retriever is trained, what an agent remembers) are now being tested against alternatives, so the default pipeline is no longer a safe assumption.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you run conversational memory over a raw transcript, rerun your own recall evals against a compacted-facts variant before changing anything; treat these papers as hypotheses until reproduced on your data.

status.detail: Three arXiv papers in nine days probe different RAG layers: retriever training, task refinement, and agent memory.
